purpose: Prevents attackers from exploiting forgotten, undocumented, or non-production API versions and hosts that lack the same security scrutiny as the current production API.
summary: Improper Inventory Management occurs when an organization doesn't maintain an accurate, up-to-date inventory of all API hosts, versions, and environments, leaving old or deprecated versions, staging/test deployments, or undocumented endpoints exposed with weaker security than the current production API.
expectedStatementElements: How the organization maintains an inventory of all API hosts, versions, and environments (production, staging, deprecated)
How deprecated or old API versions are retired, and whether they remain reachable after retirement
Whether non-production hosts (staging, dev, test) are exposed to the internet with the same or weaker security than production
How third-party or integrated systems that expose parts of the API are tracked and included in the inventory
evidenceExamples: Current API inventory documenting all hosts, versions, and environments
Deprecation policy and evidence that retired API versions are actually decommissioned
Network scan or asset discovery results confirming no unknown/undocumented API hosts are exposed
Documentation of third-party integrations that expose or consume parts of the API
commonGaps: No single, current inventory exists of all API versions and hosts across environments
Deprecated API versions remain live and reachable after being 'replaced,' with weaker security controls
Staging or test environments are internet-accessible with the same data access as production but lighter security
Third-party integrations expose API functionality that isn't tracked in the organization's own inventory
interviewQuestions: Is there one current inventory of every API version and host, or does that knowledge live in people's heads?
When an API version is deprecated, is it actually taken offline, or does it just stop being promoted?
Are any staging or test environments reachable from the internet, and if so, are they held to the same security standard?
How would you find out if a forgotten or undocumented API endpoint was still exposed somewhere?
